title: Coherence value and human bearing: the Grundrisse of Synthetic Coherence
description: These claims propose coherence value as a fifth historical value-form (#18) and hold that synthetic output carries value only by drawing on human bearing at some node of production. The Grundrisse of Synthetic Coherence (#478) states when V_Inv, Coherence Value and the W-Circuit would be disproven and argues that Marx's Fragment could not foresee cost migrating from production to reception. Related claims on scholarly labor (#751), the Groundskeeper's constitutional bloat (#533), Berners-Lee (#623) and Guillory (#819) set out falsifiability conditions and owed measurements. The page also holds five unrelated claims, among them the Blind Poet schema and the Socratic prior.

claims.statement: **[Falsifiability]** V_Inv would be disproven if a stable economy were demonstrated in which synthetic labor—produced at zero existential cost—served as durable value-backing without parasitizing human bearing at any point in the production chain (including training data, curation, evaluation, and maintenance). The qualification "at any point" is necessary because synthetic output may appear to have value-backing while parasitizing human bearing at upstream nodes—training data from human artists, curation by human editors, evaluation by human users. A genuine counterexample would require no human bearing at any node.

claims.statement: Marx's Fragment stops at a threshold it cannot cross. Marx could not imagine a form of value that was not socially necessary labor-time. The general intellect appears to him as potential liberation from labor because he assumes that once labor is automated, the "watchman and regulator" role would require no existential cost. He could not foresee that the cost would migrate from *production* to *reception*—the somatic labor of processing, evaluating, curating, and bearing infinite synthetic output.
